narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 52.9% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt—a risk slightly above the threshold used in the review. The strongest factor driving the prediction was your third-year class rank: you were in the lowest decile, far below the average accepted student near the sixth decile, and this pushed the prediction most strongly toward bar-exam failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.00, slightly below the accepted average of 3.23, was the second most influential factor, but in this case it worked in your favor and pushed toward passing. The third factor, your upper-middle family-income background, also worked in your favor; it is the most common income bracket among accepted students. These favorable factors were not enough to offset the concern raised by your very low third-year class rank.

To proceed, ask admissions for specific feedback and explain any context behind your rank. Strengthen your academic record through upper-level law coursework or a structured bar-preparation program, consider retaking the LSAT if you can improve it, and apply to programs that review candidates holistically. A higher recent academic performance and a clear study plan would give reviewers stronger evidence that your bar-exam risk has changed.
